note: Entity Access by Role Field provides a field type entity_access_by_role_field whose values are role_id + access (allowed|forbidden), enforced by hook_entity_access (entity_access_by_role_field_entity_access). Per field instance you set 'operations' (subset of view/update/delete; edit=update) and 'empty_roles_access_fallback' (neutral|allowed|forbidden). One restricted permission 'bypass entity_access_by_role_field permissions'. No configure route. It does NOT alter Views queries. All medium/hard cases are grounded in real field-instance config on node.article: introspection reads back a field's fallback and operations settings; execution changes a field's fallback and creates a new field of the type, verified against live FieldConfig. Fields are namespaced field_eabrf_*.

evals.prompt: How does the Drupal module entity_access_by_role_field decide whether a user can access an entity? What field does it add and which access hook enforces it?
evals.expected_output: It adds a field of type entity_access_by_role_field holding role_id + access (allowed/forbidden) pairs, and enforces it in hook_entity_access() (entity_access_by_role_field_entity_access), intersecting the entity's selected roles with the current user's roles.

evals.prompt: When configuring an 'Entity Access by Role' field instance in entity_access_by_role_field, which two per-field settings control which operations are governed and what happens when no role is selected? Give their setting keys and possible values.
evals.expected_output: operations (a subset of view/update/delete; edit is 'update') and empty_roles_access_fallback (neutral | allowed | forbidden).

evals.prompt: Which permission lets a user skip all of entity_access_by_role_field's per-entity access checks, and what does it do?
evals.expected_output: The restricted permission 'bypass entity_access_by_role_field permissions' — a user who has it is always allowed and the field logic is short-circuited.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an Entity Access by Role field named field_eabrf_fb. When a content editor leaves its roles empty, what access fallback applies? Inspect the live field configuration.

On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an Entity Access by Role field named field_eabrf_ops. Which entity operations does that field actually control access for? Inspect the live field configuration.
evals.expected_output: Only 'view' — field.field.node.article.field_eabrf_ops settings.operations has view enabled while update and delete are '0'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article content type has an Entity Access by Role field field_eabrf_task. Change its instance setting so that when no role is selected on an entity, access is denied (the empty-roles fallback becomes 'forbidden'). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: field.field.node.article.field_eabrf_task settings.empty_roles_access_fallback is set to 'forbidden' (e.g. load the FieldConfig, setSetting('empty_roles_access_fallback','forbidden') and save).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add an 'Entity Access by Role' field named field_eabrf_new to the Article content type so editors can control per-node role access. Create the field storage and instance on the live site.
evals.expected_output: A FieldStorageConfig node.field_eabrf_new of type entity_access_by_role_field plus a FieldConfig on node.article exist (e.g. FieldStorageConfig::create([...'type'=>'entity_access_by_role_field'])->save() then FieldConfig::create([...bundle 'article'])->save()).
